dataset.title: Audited pages
dataset.description: One row per page. status is OK when the row carries a real audit, or NOT_CHECKED_* with the reason in plain words: INVALID (the line is not an http url), DUPLICATE (the same url came earlier), LIMIT (beyond maxPages), PRIVATE_ADDRESS (a host name really answered with a non public address, whether the page host, a redirect hop or a host the page loads from; a redirect and a loaded resource are recognised after the browser has already asked, and such a row is never charged, while a name that does not resolve at all is not a private address and does not block the page), DNS_ERROR (the host name does not resolve or is not a valid host name), TIMEOUT (the page did not finish loading in pageTimeoutSecs), HTTP_ERROR (the page answered 4xx or 5xx), NOT_HTML (the response is a pdf, an image or anything else that is not a page), PROBE_ERROR (Chromium could not read the page), and TIME, CAP, BILLING and ERROR when the run stopped before this page for the reason in the summary. The signals: title and titleLength, metaDescription and metaDescriptionLength, h1 with the first heading text, h1Count, h2Count, h3Count, canonical, metaRobots, noindex, nofollow, htmlLang, viewport, charset, ogCount with ogTitle and ogImage, twitterCount, jsonLdBlocks with jsonLdTypes and jsonLdInvalid, images and imagesMissingAlt, internalLinks, externalLinks, nofollowLinks, emptyAnchors, hreflangCount, wordCount, bodyChars. The judgement: seoScore from 0 to 100, seoGrade (good at 80 and above, needs-improvement from 50 to 79, poor below 50), issues as a list of code, severity, points, message and fix, with issueCount, criticalIssues, warningIssues, noticeIssues and penalty. The penalty is the sum of the points of the issues, so 100 minus the penalty gives the score back. httpStatus, contentType, finalUrl and redirects say where the browser ended up. resourceHosts lists at most 25 host names the page loads from, resourceHostsTotal is how many were seen and resourceHostsTruncated says the list was cut. billable is a claim about the price list; the money actually taken is chargedEvents in the summary.

summary.title: Run summary
summary.description: Run summary. requested is how many lines were sent, blank lines included; processed plus notChecked always equals requested. delivered counts OK rows, rowsWritten counts every row written, chargedEvents is what the platform charged, billingActive says whether this run could bill at all and billingReason says why not. chargedEvents and delivered are the same number unless a charge failed: deliveredUncharged counts those rows and chargeErrors the attempts, writeErrors counts rows the dataset refused. stopReason is null, spending-cap, charge-error, dataset-write-error, deadline, billing-price-unknown or unexpected-error, and unexpectedError carries the reason for the last one. byStatus is the full breakdown, byGrade counts good, needs-improvement and poor pages. duplicateTitles counts pages whose title repeats an earlier page of this run and pagesWithDuplicateTitle counts the titles involved, because one page cannot see that problem on its own. cutByMaxPages is the tail the limit cut and maxPages the limit actually applied. deadlineCapped says the clock stopped the run and pageMarginSecs is the margin that check used. privateBlocked counts every page the address guard stopped, privateSubresourceBlocked the part that came from a loaded resource, dnsErrors the host names that did not resolve, subresourceDnsSkipped the loaded names that did not resolve at all and so blocked nothing, pagesWithTruncatedHostList the pages whose host list was cut at 25 names, subresourceHostLookups how many names the guard resolved; httpErrors, notHtml, timeouts and probeErrors count the other free rows by cause. datasetItemCount is our own count of written rows, datasetItemCountApi the same as the platform reported it, datasetItemCountNote explains a gap. The named store keeps one object per run under RUN_SUMMARY-<runId>.
